The ISA reference is correct: pulp_v2.hpp:1930 p_clipi_exec clamps to [-(1<<(imm-1)), (1<<(imm-1))-1]; :1987 p_extracti_exec and :1996 p_extractui_exec use width=imm+1. The upstream pattern is followed: the clip fix uses the same trailing-ones-plus-one-of-upper-bound transform as CORE-V cv.clip (RISCVInstrInfoXCV.td:723-728, :771-773 @llvmorg-20.1.8) and as the fork's own p.clipu and clip-idiom patterns (RISCVInstrInfoXpulp.td:1255-1256, :1847-1848).

Diff (RISCVInstrInfoXpulp.td only, +15/-7): the int_riscv_pulp_clip pattern now encodes trailing1sPlus1_pulp(upperBound) instead of trailing0s(lowerBound). The bextract/bextractu patterns now take a new TImmLeaf bitFieldWidth (1..32) and a new SDNodeXForm minus1. Every line is needed for the root cause (builtin immediate not converted to the ISA field encoding). No fork logic is removed, no early returns, no forced conditions, no deleted patterns, no unrelated edits.

GCC oracle (independent sweep, my own generator): I compiled 304 functions with build/20-F002 clang and GAP9 GCC -march=rv32imcxgap9 -O2: clip [-2^n,2^n-1] and clipu [0,2^n-1] for n=0..29 (the whole GCC-accepted range), bextract/bextractu for every Size 1..32 at offsets {0,1,5,32-Size}, plus bset/bclr at edge masks (0x1, 0xff00, ~0x80000000). 207 are instruction-identical. The other 97 are all bextract[u] cases that GCC folds to an equivalent sra/srl/p.bclr/p.extbs/p.exthz/andi or to nothing (Size=32, Off=0); I checked each class and all are semantically equal. None of the 97 is a p.clip/p.clipu/p.bset/p.bclr difference.

clipu/clipr/clipur/binsert/bset/bclr are unaffected: their patterns are unchanged in the diff, and clipu matches GCC for n=0..29, bset/bclr match GCC. clip_r/clipu_r map to register forms (GVSoC :1949/:1958). binsert uses the unchanged maskWidthMinus1 xform (GCC's binsert builtin has a different signature, so I did not compare its output directly).

bextract Size=0 now fails with the backend fatal 'Cannot select' instead of silently extracting 1 bit. This is acceptable for this task. Size=0 is invalid input: GCC rejects it in the front end ('Size>0'), and p.extract cannot encode a 0-bit field. Silent wrong code for invalid input was the worse behaviour, and 'Cannot select' was already what the fork did for another invalid-encoding value (Size=32, before this fix). No in-tree test or SDK kernel uses Size=0. The proper diagnostic belongs to Sema (SemaRISCV.cpp:1422, range [0,32] -> [1,32]). That is the clang-builtins cluster, a different owner cluster and a separate change under rule 5, so it should be a follow-up task and must not be folded into this one.

Edge case the worker did not report (non-blocking, follow-up): __builtin_pulp_clip(x, INT_MIN, INT_MAX) now gives Is2 = countr_one(0x7fffffff)+1 = 32, which does not fit uimm5. In a release build it encodes as 0 (clamp to [-1,0]); -verify-machineinstrs reports 'Bad machine code: Invalid immediate'. Before the fix it gave p.clip 31, which is also wrong (clamp to +-2^30). __builtin_pulp_clipu(x,0,INT_MAX) already had this hole before the fix, and the ref-18 toolchain has it too (p.clipu 32). Upstream CORE-V powerOf2Minus1/trailing1sPlus1 has the same unguarded range. GCC rejects these bounds (it accepts only n<=29 for clip/clipu). The right fix is the Sema follow-up: require lo == -(hi+1) for clip (worker's other_errors_seen item 1) and cap hi at 2^30-1 so Is2<=31 for clip and clipu. Recommended scope for that clang-builtins task: clip lo==-(hi+1), clip/clipu hi<=2^30-1, bextract[u] Size>=1.
